label: Bible Study
prompt: Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the _____ of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready.
verse: Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready.
note: Heaven announces the wedding of the Lamb — and the bride has made herself ready.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in _____, as we have received a commandment from the Father.
verse: I rejoiced greatly that I found of thy children walking in truth, as we have received a commandment from the Father.
note: The elder's happiest news: finding some of the children walking in truth.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the _____ lay.
verse: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.
note: Friends dug through a roof to lower the man down — 'sick of the palsy' is the KJV's way of saying paralysed.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the LORD will work for us: for there is no _____ to the LORD to save by many or by few.
verse: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the LORD will work for us: for there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.
note: Jonathan and his armorbearer took on a Philistine garrison alone: God can save by many or by few.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as _____ between thine eyes.
verse: And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes.
note: Bind God's words on your hand and as 'frontlets between thine eyes' — the root of the phylacteries mentioned in Matthew 23:5.
